Here is my k-means.R
kmeans.mr = 
function(
P,
num.clusters,
num.iter,
combine,
in.memory.combine){

C = NULL
for(i in 1:num.iter){

C = 
values(
from.dfs(
mapreduce(
P,
input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
map = kmeans.map,
reduce = kmeans.reduce)))
if(combine || in.memory.combine)
C = C[,-1]/C[,1]

if(nrow(C) < num.clusters){
C = 
rbind(
C,
matrix(
rnorm(
(num.clusters - nrow(C)) * nrow(C)),
ncol = nrow(C)) %*% C)
}
}

C
}

dist.fun = 
function(C, P){
apply(C, 1, function(x) colSums((t(P) - x)^2))
}

kmeans.map = 
function(., P){
nearest = {
if(is.null(C)){
sample(
1:num.clusters,
nrow(P),
replace = T)
}
else{
D = dist.fun(C, P)
nearest = max.col(-D)
}
}
if(!(combine || in.memory.combine))
keyval(nearest, P)
else
keyval(nearest, cbind(1, P))
}

kmeans.reduce = 
function(., P){
if(!(combine || in.memory.combine))
function(., P)
t(as.matrix(apply(P, 2, mean)))
else
function(k, P)
keyval(k, t(as.matrix(apply(P, 2, sum))))
}

kmeans.mr(
"hdfs://cloud001:9000/user/23G/23G/cluster",
num.clusters = 4,
num.iter = 5,
combine = FALSE,
in.memory.combine = FALSE)

Version Info:
Hadoop 2.2.0
R 3.0.1

What am I doing wrong?
Thanks!

Yes.

It has been brought to my attention that the last answer was somewhat terse. The general idea is that I don't take on custom programming jobs here. You are asking to expand an example  packages with rmr2 in a particular direction of reading a different format. This seems something the core devs shouldn't be taking on and a perfect learning opportunity. Read help(mapreduce), input.format in particular, and help(make.input.format) and give it a try. Start on the local backend for ease of debugging. Learn R first. I hope this helps.
 


Antonio
